stories.headline: Mediators say 'positive progress' made in US-Iran talks in Doha
stories.summary: Mediators from Qatar and Pakistan have concluded separate meetings with US and Iranian negotiators in Doha, reporting "positive progress" on issues related to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. The meetings built on the outcomes of the Lake Lucerne Summit, with both sides agreeing to continue discussions. US officials, including Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, had positive conversations with regional leaders in Doha earlier in the week. The talks, facilitated by Qatari mediators, aimed to discuss developments and move forward on issues tied to the memorandum of understanding. The progress made is seen as a step forward in the US-Iran talks, with both countries committing to continue the dialogue. The exact details of the progress made have not been disclosed, but the mediators' statement suggests a positive momentum in the negotiations. Further discussions are expected to take place in the coming days.

stories.headline: Ivory Coast: Nearly 60 people killed in flooding since May
stories.summary: Nearly 60 people have been killed in flooding in Ivory Coast since May, according to a government spokesperson. The country's rainy season, which runs from May to late July, has brought "particularly heavy" rainfall, leading to deadly flooding and landslides. Informal settlements are especially vulnerable to flooding, and searches of affected areas are ongoing. In the capital, Abidjan, 10 people were killed in floods in just two days. Authorities fear the toll could rise as the rainy season is only just beginning. The government reported the deaths at a cabinet meeting, highlighting the annual risk of flooding and landslides in the country, especially in less-developed areas. The flooding has already surpassed typical annual levels, with dozens killed in a short period.

stories.headline: More than 100 sick in severe multi-country Salmonella outbreak
stories.summary: A multi-country Salmonella outbreak in Europe has resulted in 106 confirmed cases across 14 countries between November 2025 and June 2026. The primary food vehicle is believed to be alfalfa sprouts and possibly other sprouted seeds, although flavored-noodle products have also been linked to the outbreak. European food safety and health officials have reported that evidence points to a specific brand of flavored-noodle products as the likely source of the infections. The cases are connected to the Salmonella Stanley strain, which has been linked to a producer in Ukraine. The outbreak has affected 13 European countries, with the number of sick individuals exceeding 100. Officials continue to investigate the outbreak to determine the exact cause and scope of the contamination. The affected countries and the specific vendor have not been disclosed.

stories.headline: Taiwan condemns China's vessel deployments near its waters
stories.summary: Taiwan has condemned China's deployment of government vessels to waters surrounding the island, including off its east coast. The move is seen as an effort by China to normalize its operational presence in the area. Two Chinese vessels briefly entered restricted waters near Taiwan-controlled Itu Aba Island, prompting a strong criticism from Taiwan's Coast Guard Administration. The vessels reportedly left Taiwan's waters early Monday. In response, Taiwan's government has pledged to maintain close coordination between the military and Coast Guard to safeguard maritime security. Taiwan has also instructed its ships to ignore boarding requests by China's coast guard. The incident highlights the ongoing tensions between Taiwan and China, with Taiwan seeking to protect its sovereignty and maritime interests. The situation is being closely monitored by Taiwan's authorities to ensure the island's security and stability.

stories.headline: Billions of Phones Could Be Exposed to Nearby Attacks Through AirDrop and Quick Share
stories.summary: Researchers have discovered six security flaws in AirDrop and Quick Share, features used by over five billion iPhones and Android phones. These vulnerabilities allow nearby hackers to cause crashes, tamper with active transfers, and potentially run code on affected devices without needing pairing, prompts, or prior access. The flaws span across iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows, affecting protocols on a massive scale. Specifically, the bugs can bypass Samsung's session checks and trigger a crash in Google's Windows app. The vulnerabilities expose devices to attacks from strangers in close proximity, putting users at risk. The researchers have probed the protocols and disclosed the security flaws, highlighting the need for defenders to take action to protect against these potential threats. The affected features are used for file sharing, leaving users vulnerable to nearby attacks.

stories.headline: Apple readies new iPad Pro and redesigned MacBook Pro for 2027: Here's everything you need to know
stories.summary: Apple is preparing to release new iPad Pro models and a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro in the first half of 2027. The upcoming MacBook Pro, codenamed K104, will feature a new design and is expected to be powered by Apple's first M7 processor. This follows the release of a base MacBook Pro model, codenamed J804, which is due late 2026 and runs on an M6 chip with the existing design. The new iPad Pro lineup and MacBook Pro are part of a slate of major new products planned for 2027, marking the iPhone's 20th anniversary year. According to Bloomberg, Apple is currently testing these new devices, with the M7 processor also expected to debut in early 2027. The redesigned MacBook Pro and upgraded iPad Pro models are anticipated to be significant updates to Apple's product line.

stories.headline: Vinton Cerf Says AI Must Learn These 3 Lessons
stories.summary: Vinton Cerf, one of the "Fathers of the Internet" and Google's outgoing Chief Internet Evangelist, spoke at the Open Frontier conference on June 30, 2026. He emphasized that AI agents will need common technical standards to work safely and efficiently with each other. Cerf predicted that the rise of autonomous agents will lead the AI industry to adopt formal, standardized protocols, as natural language is too ambiguous for reliable communication. He highlighted three key lessons for AI to learn from the internet: standardization, abstraction layers to separate concerns, and the end-to-end principle, which keeps the core simple and pushes intelligence to the edge. By applying these principles, the AI industry can foster innovation and avoid building monolithic AI stacks, similar to the internet's development. Cerf's insights come from his experience as a co-architect of the internet and his 20-year tenure at Google.

stories.headline: Technology alone is not enough
stories.summary: Technology alone is insufficient to address broader challenges, according to recent discussions. A panel noted that data quality, comparability, and reporting issues cannot be solved by technology alone. Similarly, experts warn that technology will not be enough to save the food system, despite advancements in predicting food crises. In the context of commerce, trust is a crucial factor in the adoption of new technologies, such as AI-powered commerce. While 84% of consumers in Saudi Arabia believe AI will play a critical role in protecting them from fraud, trust in digital environments is necessary for widespread adoption. Additionally, China has surpassed the US in 57 of 64 priority technologies, highlighting the need for a multifaceted approach beyond just technological advancements. A comprehensive strategy that incorporates trust, security, and other factors is necessary for success.

stories.headline: Senegal 'Devastated' after Late World Cup Collapse Against Belgium
stories.summary: Senegal's World Cup campaign ended in devastating fashion with a late collapse against Belgium in the round of 32. The match, played in Seattle, saw Senegal's hopes dashed despite advancing to the knockout phase as one of the best third-place finishers. They had lost to France and Norway, but beaten Iraq, to reach this stage. The team is left reeling, with players expressing disappointment and blame. A penalty awarded to Belgium contributed to Senegal's downfall. The team's goalkeeper, Mory Diaw, and other players were visibly distraught after the loss. Senegal's coach and players acknowledged that they only had themselves to blame for the defeat, citing a lack of effort and commitment during the 90-minute match. The loss has left the team "devastated" and struggling to come to terms with their World Cup exit.

stories.headline: Romelu Lukaku plays peacemaker as Belgium teammates clash before stunning World Cup comeback vs Senegal
stories.summary: Belgium staged a stunning World Cup comeback against Senegal, with Romelu Lukaku playing a key role as peacemaker and goalscorer. As the game entered its final minutes, Belgian players became frustrated with each other, but Lukaku intervened to calm tensions. His efforts paid off as he netted in the 86th minute, followed by Tielemans' equalizing strike three minutes later. The dramatic turnaround marked Belgium's second improbable comeback in their last 11 World Cup games. The win was preceded by a tense moment when Lukaku had to wait to take a kick as Senegal players surrounded the spot, but he remained calm and dispatched the effort. The incident highlighted the emotional state of the Belgian dressing room, with Lukaku's peacekeeping efforts proving crucial in the team's victory. The comeback win keeps Belgium's World Cup hopes alive.

stories.headline: ‘Vaibhav Sooryavanshi would have taken their pants off’: Vintage Ravi Shastri gets brutally honest
stories.summary: Ravi Shastri, former India coach, has criticized the team's decision to delay 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's T20I debut. Shastri believes Sooryavanshi should have played against Ireland, citing the youngster's "X-factor" and fearlessness. He emphasized Sooryavanshi's potential to make an impact, saying he would have "taken their pants off" with his aggressive batting style, particularly on the small ground in Ireland. Shastri's comments contrast with the team management's preference for experienced openers to maintain stability and continuity. The former coach remains adamant that Sooryavanshi's debut should not have been delayed, highlighting the 15-year-old's exuberance and potential to make a significant contribution to the team. Shastri's blunt assessment has sparked debate about Sooryavanshi's future in the Indian cricket team.

stories.headline: Banned Eddie backs student flyhalf
stories.summary: Japan has named uncapped student fly-half Ryunosuke Ito to start against Italy in their Nations Championship opener in Tokyo. Notably, head coach Eddie Jones will be absent from the touchline due to a ban. Despite his absence, Jones has expressed support for the young player. The match marks the beginning of the Nations Championship, with Japan aiming to make a strong start. Jones, who is banned, has made light of his situation, jokingly saying he is "looking for a laundry basket," implying he will be watching from a distance. The Brave Blossoms will face Italy without their coach's direct guidance, relying on their preparedness and team strategy to secure a win. The Nations Championship is a significant tournament, and Japan's performance will be closely watched.

stories.headline: Rs 35,000-crore investment push linked to Maruti plant during Japan PM's visit
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki has earmarked a total investment of Rs 35,000 crore for India, which includes the supplier ecosystem. The investment is linked to the company's new plant in Kharkhoda, Haryana, set to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The Kharkhoda plant is Maruti Suzuki's fourth manufacturing facility and is expected to generate over 21,000 direct jobs. The investment is a significant milestone in the company's journey towards achieving an annual capacity of 40 lakh units over the next few years. The Rs 35,000 crore investment demonstrates long-term confidence in India's market and underscores the country's attractiveness as a manufacturing hub. The new plant will contribute to Maruti Suzuki's expansion plans and reinforce its position in the Indian automotive industry.

stories.headline: Bengaluru creche abuse: Toddlers locked in washing machine, bathrooms
stories.summary: Bengaluru police have registered a case against five women employed at a daycare centre inside the Capgemini IT company campus after videos showed toddlers being physically and mentally abused. The abuse included locking the children in bathrooms and making them sit inside a front-loading washing machine. The videos also showed caregivers spraying water into the toddlers' mouths and physically assaulting them, leaving the children crying. An investigation has been launched, and the police are probing the allegations. The daycare centre is located on the Capgemini campus, and the incident has sparked outrage. The five women booked are caregivers at the centre, and further investigation is underway to determine the extent of the abuse and ensure the safety of the children. The police are reviewing the videos and gathering more evidence to build a case against the accused.

stories.headline: Bengaluru horror: Toddlers locked in washing machines, forced into pipes at IT campus creche
stories.summary: A daycare center at the Capgemini IT campus in Bengaluru is under investigation for alleged abuse of toddlers. Five female staff members have been booked for physically and mentally harassing children aged 2-3 years. The accused allegedly locked crying children inside washing machines, forced them into narrow water-filled pipes, and confined them in bathroom spaces to intimidate them. They also physically assaulted the children. The allegations came to light after a complaint was filed, prompting an FIR against the staff members. The incident has sparked outrage and raised concerns about the safety and well-being of children in daycare centers. The accused staff members are being investigated for their actions, which are said to have caused severe trauma to the affected children. The IT company has not commented on the incident, but an investigation is underway.

stories.headline: Capgemini temporarily shuts Bengaluru daycare after videos show inhumane treatment of toddlers
stories.summary: Capgemini has temporarily shut its daycare facility at its Bengaluru campus after videos surfaced showing toddlers being subjected to alleged inhumane treatment by caregivers. The footage sparked widespread outrage, leading to a police investigation and an FIR against five women. The company is cooperating with authorities and has closed the facility pending the investigation. The videos allegedly showed caregivers mistreating toddlers, including spraying water into their mouths with a toilet jet. The incident has triggered a probe into possible repeated mistreatment of children at the daycare centre. Capgemini has stated that it is taking the matter seriously and is working with the authorities to ensure the well-being and safety of the children. The police investigation is ongoing, and the company's actions are aimed at addressing the concerns raised by the disturbing videos.

stories.headline: The Volvo EX30 Cross Country review: A victim of geopolitics
stories.summary: The Volvo EX30 Cross Country, a subcompact EV, has been impacted by geopolitics, particularly US tariffs on Chinese-made cars. In response, Volvo shifted production to its Belgian factory, but the resulting 25% tariff increased the starting price to $40,345 for the rear-wheel drive version and $46,345 for the all-wheel drive version. The EX30 Cross Country adds more ground clearance, cladding, and underbody protection, making it suitable for various environments. However, the model's momentum was hindered by a global recall due to overheating concerns, affecting around 372 units locally, with one reported fire incident in Johannesburg. Despite this, the Cross Country version was introduced in late 2025, potentially catering to US preferences for SUV-style vehicles. The EX30's digital-centric cabin has become less jarring over time, but the tariffs and recalls have affected the model's overall prospects.

stories.headline: Tariffs and anti-China policies killed this little Volvo in the United States.
stories.summary: Volvo is discontinuing the EX30 in the United States after the 2026 model year due to tariffs on imported vehicles and slowing EV sales growth. The decision is largely attributed to the 100% tariffs imposed on Chinese-made EVs in the US. Volvo, majority-owned by Chinese automaker Geely, had initially produced the EX30 in China but later moved production to avoid the tariffs. Despite this effort, the model's sales were still impacted, leading to its discontinuation in the US market. The EX30's demise illustrates the significant effect of tariff policies on automotive products. Volvo's US lineup is becoming more limited as a result, with the company adjusting its production and sales strategies to mitigate the impact of tariffs and anti-China policies. The XC60 model will now be built in the US to avoid similar issues.

stories.headline: Stock markets today: Sensex, Nifty rally as crude oil prices decline, IT stocks gain
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rallied in early trade, driven by a decline in crude oil prices and positive geopolitical developments. The drop in oil prices was fueled by hopes of a US-Iran conflict resolution. As a result, IT stocks gained, contributing to the overall market uptrend. The Sensex and Nifty50 ended the session on a strong note, reversing previous losses. The Indian stock market had previously extended sharp losses for three consecutive sessions due to rising worries over escalating US-Iran tensions and a rally in oil prices. However, the current decline in oil prices has eased investor concerns, leading to a positive trend in the stock market. The latest stock market updates and movements can be tracked on financial news platforms, providing insights into the Indian and global markets.

stories.headline: Indian Equities Extend Gains as Crude Prices Ease, IT Stocks Surge
stories.summary: Indian stock markets extended their rally for a second day, with the Sensex and Nifty indices seeing significant gains. The surge was driven by easing crude oil prices, which fell below $73 per barrel, and strong performance from IT sector stocks. A strengthening rupee also boosted investor enthusiasm. The Sensex climbed over 800 points to close at 76,991.22, marking a significant increase of 790 points. The rally defied a global tech sell-off, with Indian benchmark indices extending their gains for the fourth consecutive day. The IT sector played a key role in the surge, along with the banking sector, which also saw robust gains. The decline in crude oil costs and softened Brent crude prices, which settled at multi-month lows, contributed to the market's upward momentum. The Indian stock market's rally was driven by a combination of positive factors, leading to a significant increase in investor confidence.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today (July 2, 2026): Sensex, Nifty Open Firm, Trade Higher
stories.summary: Indian benchmark equity indices, Sensex and Nifty, opened higher on July 2, 2026, tracking positive global cues and firm investor sentiment. The BSE Sensex traded at 77,180.01, up 257.37 points or 0.33%, while Nifty climbed 0.35% or 86 points to 24,092.05. In early trade, the Sensex surged 0.38% or about 300 points to hit an intraday high of 77,218.78. Market breadth was positive, with 1,981 stocks advancing against 771 stocks declining on the NSE. The IT sector emerged as the top gainer, with the Nifty IT index jumping over 3%. The positive sentiment was also influenced by a decline in crude oil prices, with Brent crude falling 1.09% to $70.79 and US WTI falling 1.27% to $67.71 per barrel. The overall technical setup remains positive with a bullish undertone.

stories.headline: Sensex Today | Stock Market Live: GIFT Nifty hints a strong start; US, Asian markets fall
stories.summary: The Indian stock market is expected to start strong, with the GIFT Nifty hinting at a positive opening. stories.headline: [The Hindu] Why Deutsche Bank exiting India retail business | Explained
stories.summary: Deutsche Bank is exiting its retail banking business in India, selling its assets to Kotak Mahindra Bank. The German lender had invited bids from domestic and foreign lenders, and Kotak Mahindra Bank has emerged as the preferred buyer. The acquisition, valued at Rs 4,500 crore, will enhance Kotak's retail loan and deposit portfolio, including MSME lending and wealth management assets. Deutsche Bank's decision to sell its India retail business comes amid rising competition and cost-cutting efforts. The bank's wealth management operations in India have seen a sharp decline, with assets under management (AUM) falling from $4 billion to $1 billion. The sale will allow Deutsche Bank to streamline its focus on core operations, while strengthening Kotak Mahindra Bank's position in the Indian retail banking sector. The acquisition includes 17 branches and will expand Kotak's presence in the market.

stories.headline: [ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation] Australia ranks third-highest for median wealth globally, UBS data shows
stories.summary: Australia ranks third-highest for median wealth globally, with a median wealth of $306,074, according to the 2025 UBS Global Wealth Report. The country is surpassed only by Luxembourg and Belgium. The report attributes the high ranking to recent surges in property values, which have boosted the number of Australian millionaires. Australia has jumped from the 10th wealthiest population to the third in just one year, driven by a surge in super assets. The UBS report shows that the median Australian is among the wealthiest in the world, with the country having the second-highest median wealth. The significant increase in wealth is a result of the growth in property values and superannuation assets, solidifying Australia's position as one of the wealthiest countries globally. The report highlights the country's rapid rise in global wealth rankings.

stories.headline: [NZ Herald] based telco NOW’s closure follows ‘24 years of success’, founding chairman says
stories.summary: Napier-based internet and telco business NOW is closing after 24 years, resulting in 70 job losses across its New Zealand centres. The company, founded as Airnet in 2002, provided internet services in Hawke's Bay and expanded over the years. Founding chairman attributed the closure to the end of a successful 24-year run. The business has been operating in New Zealand, offering various telecommunication services. The closure will impact employees across the company's centres in the country. The founding chairman reflected on the company's history, acknowledging its achievements over the past two decades. The closure of NOW marks the end of an era for the regional telco, which had been a part of the local community for nearly a quarter of a century.

stories.headline: [The Hindu] is not the most relevant, replacing with none, the fourth most relevant is [The Straits Times] 2 arrested, 4 others taken to hospital after alleged brawl in Orchard Road
stories.summary: 2 individuals were arrested and 4 others taken to the hospital after an alleged brawl occurred in Orchard Road. The incident led to a significant disruption, with emergency responders facing challenges due to thick smoke engulfing the building's enclosed interiors. The lack of alternative emergency exits or external evacuation routes severely hampered rescue efforts. The situation was brought under control after the arrests and hospitalizations. The cause of the brawl and the extent of the injuries are not specified. The incident is being investigated, and further details are expected to be released. The Orchard Road area is a popular destination in Singapore, known for its shopping and entertainment options, and the incident has raised concerns about safety and emergency preparedness in the area.

stories.headline: OpenAI and Anthropic Built AI Around Tokens. Palantir's Karp Says 'Something Has Gone Completely Wrong' With The Model.
stories.summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp has criticized the token-based pricing model used by OpenAI and Anthropic, stating that it encourages companies to spend heavily on AI tokens without delivering meaningful value. Karp argued that enterprises are growing frustrated with this model, seeking cheaper and more efficient alternatives. He claimed that "something has gone completely wrong" with OpenAI and Anthropic, highlighting tensions and scrutiny around leading AI companies. Karp promoted Palantir and Nvidia's open model as a solution for enterprises and governments seeking to own their data. This criticism comes as businesses are looking for cost-effective AI solutions, and Karp's remarks put a spotlight on the pricing models used by major AI companies, sparking debate about the value and efficiency of token-based systems. Karp's comments were made during an appearance on CNBC.

stories.headline: AI #175: The Fable Continues
stories.summary: Claude Fable 5, an AI model, has achieved a significant milestone by completing 16.1% of projects at a professional standard, roughly double the next model. This advancement has raised concerns about balancing AI innovation with national security requirements and safeguards to prevent misuse. Following discussions between Anthropic and US officials, export controls were lifted on June 30, and Fable 5 was made available on July 1. The model's temporary unavailability was due to an incident that sparked debates about AI security and government intervention. Experts argue that the incident reflects a universal limitation in AI models, while critics claim the White House overreacted, setting a dangerous precedent. Anthropic maintains that the reported behavior supports defensive security work, and the company is moving forward with plans to release GPT-5.6, a new model built on the same framework.
